h.strategy: Most obvious hypotheses follow a local story: an option matters more when its substitute is missing. These are usually rated likely and often fail. Instead, base hypotheses on robust statistical regularities. (1) Headroom: helpful edits help less in parents that are already strong, for example parents that already contain the strongest option elsewhere. (2) Harmful edits hurt more in strong parents and look harmless in weak parents, because of floor effects. (3) Saturation: adding a second copy of a strong option gives smaller gains than adding the first. (4) Removing an option costs less when the parent has several similar options. Choose conditions that many parents satisfy, so the effect is detectable. Cover several edited fields and both directions. In each 'why', state the obvious prediction and the reason the opposite should hold.

hyps.why: Obvious: dropping edge 4 hurts regardless; but a skip on the direct edge keeps a gradient path and similar connectivity, so removal costs less when it is present.
Obvious: removing an internal edge costs the same regardless of siblings; but a conv3x3 on edge 1 already supplies node 2 with a strong path, so removing edge 2 costs less.
Obvious: edge 0 is needed to feed node 1 and its removal always hurts; but another conv from the input is a similar option, so removal is cheaper when it is present.
Obvious: a skip on the direct edge gives a gradient shortcut everywhere; but its benefit is largest in weak parents, and a conv3x3 into the output already makes the cell strong.
Obvious: a strong sibling edge makes removing edge 5 cheaper; but removal is harmless in weak parents (floor effect) and costs more in strong parents with more accuracy to lose.
Obvious: a strong edge 4 masks a weak edit on edge 2; but replacing a good op with pooling hurts strong parents more, while weak parents are already near the floor.
Obvious: edge 1 is redundant when edge 5 is strong; but strong parents lose more from disconnecting a path than weak parents do, since weak ones are floored.
Obvious: removing edge 0 is cheap when edge 2 is strong; but a strong cell has more to lose, while weak cells show floor effects.
Obvious: another strong path into the output makes dropping the direct edge harmless; but removing the skip-like shortcut hurts strong cells more than weak ones, which are already near the floor.
Obvious: conv3x3 on edge 5 compensates for losing edge 4; but strong parents have more accuracy to lose, whereas weak parents sit near the floor and barely change.
